claim.value: When closing an inconclusive test without a predefined feasible extension, choose the next discriminating inquiry.
claim.scope: The same 'otherwise' branch as unresolved closure; no particular next inquiry is specified.

provenance.rationale: P029 explicitly prescribes choosing the next discriminating inquiry when closing the test as unresolved without a predefined feasible extension.

signal_basis.value: The release test remains inconclusive after assessing first-publication differences, uncertainty and guardrails against predefined decision requirements, and no predefined feasible extension is available.
signal_basis.scope: The selected change at the predefined endpoint, with follow-up spanning an intended roster opportunity.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply the predefined assessment requirements, observed test measures, endpoint and inconclusive-result branch.
The supported procedural claim requires no unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: An inconclusive test leaves the relevant uncertainty unresolved. When its permitted extension is unavailable, choosing a further inquiry aimed at discriminating explanations is licensed as a bounded learning decision. The claim neither identifies a particular inquiry nor guarantees that it will resolve the uncertainty.
uncertainty: The effectiveness of any subsequent inquiry remains unknown; the claim only prescribes choosing one.
